JUDGEMENT

The present suit is filed by the plaintiff- Registered Partnership Firm by its one of the O S No.8246/2016 partner Dr. Syed Anwar against the defendants seeking the relief of perpetual injunction restraining the defendants, their agents or their representatives from entering upon the suit schedule property or from interfering with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property.

2. The plaintiff has given description in respect of the suit property, which is reproduced hereunder;
All that piece and parcel of Immovable Property being the converted land forming a portion of Survey No.97/1-B, Singasandra Village, Begur Hobli, now known as and earlier bearing Khatha No.368, Property No.308/97/1B, situated in Singasandra of the City Municipal Council,
Bommanahalli, Bangalore, presently bearing BBMP Khatha No.395/368/97/1B, measuring 17.5 O S No.8246/2016 guntas or 19057.5 Sq.ft., bounded on East by -Remaining portion of the property in Sy.No.97/1B, Singasandra Village, measuring 4800 Square Feet belonging to the plaintiff, West by- Hosur Road, North by-40 Feet road and South by-Private Property in Sy.No.97/1-A.
3.

The case of the plaintiff is in nutshell as under:-
It is pleaded that the plaintiff is the absolute owner and in possession over the suit property, since it was purchased by way of registered Sale Deed dated 28-02-2006 from its erstwhile owner Mrs. R.Nalini Ashok.
The B.B.M.P. has assessed the tax and the plaintiff has been remitting the same to the BBMP.

Basically, the land Sy.No.97/1B, situated at Singasandra Village, Begur Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk,
totally measuring 0.22 guntas belonging to one Smt. O S No.8246/2016 Yediyur Muniyamma @ Ammayamma, W/o.
Late. Hanumappa Reddy.
The said land was subsequently converted into non agricultural purpose as per the order of the Deputy Commissioner, dated 21-09-1993.
The said land was earlier belonging to one Naga Reddy, who is the father-in-law of above said Yediyur Muniyamma, since he has purchased the same by way of registered Sale Deed dated 17-04-1952.

After his death,
the said 0.22 guntas land has been succeeded by his son Hanumappa Reddy, who is the husband of above said Yediyur Muniyamma.
Since the Hanumappa Reddy died therefore, Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and children Venkatesh Reddy and Purushothama Reddy succeeded the said property.

Further, it is pleaded that the said land was acquired by the Government of Karnataka in favour of Air Craft Employees House Building Co- operative Society Limited under acquisition Notification M/S. Orange Tree vs K.V.Mathew on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20441790/
3 dated 30-09-1989 (Hereinafter it is referred as Society).

sentences.text: The said Society was unable to take physical possession of above said property because, the Government of Karnataka itself could take possession.
Therefore, the said land did not vest in favour of the Society.
It means, the possession remained with Yediyur Muniyamma.

5. It is further pleaded that Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and her children had filed O.S.No.8577/1997 against the Society and later, that was amicably resolved inasmuch as the Society was not interested in the said lands so, O S No.8246/2016 Resolution dated 10-05-1999 was came to be passed in the meeting and accordingly, the Society abandoned and released all rights and claim over 0.22 guntas,
which was already converted.
Thereby, the Society issued no objection certificate on 05-06-1999 and executed Deed of Settlement dated 23-05-1999 in favour of Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma.
The land measuring 0.22 guntas, which is converted in Sy.No.97/1B has been shown in blue colour.
The said Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma gave up a claim of compensation from the Society of the lands Sy.No.97/B and 96/2, which is shown in red colour.
It is said that 40 feet road, which is formed can be used and utilised by both the parties.
The said fact has also been confirmed by the Society in a meeting held on 30-05-1999.
Therefore, Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma became the absolute owner and in possession and enjoyment over the land Sy.No.97/B comprising of 0.22 guntas shown in blue colour.

6. It is further pleaded that the said Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and her family was in legal necessity therefore, sold 17.5 guntas in the converted land Sy.No.97/1-B by way of registered Sale Deed dated 23-08-1999 in favour of one K.Damodar for a valuable sale consideration and put up him in the possession.
The BBMP has assessed the tax.
Accordingly, Sri. K.Damodar remitting the tax.

It is further pleaded that the said K.Damodar by exercising his absolute right of ownership, sold the schedule property measuring 17.5 guntas or 19057 Sq.Ft. in favour of one Mr. Sheik Mohammed Jamil and his wife O S No.8246/2016 Mrs. Malika by way of registered Sale Deed dated 20-11-2003.

The name of said purchasers came to be transferred into the khatha and they are by exercising their rights sold the said property in favour of Smt. R.Nalini Ashok by way of registered Sale Deed dated 10-09-2004.
The said Smt. R.Nalini Ashok exercising her rights over the suit schedule property, sold the same in favour of the plaintiff.
So, the plaintiff is in lawful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property.

7. It is alleged that one Sri. Thimmegowda illegally attempted to enter into the portion of suit schedule property with false assertions that site No.2533 in Block-A is said to have been allotted to him by the above said Society measuring 50 x 100 Sq.ft.
The claim of said Sri. O S No.8246/2016 Thimmegowda is baseless and utter false.
Because, he is not at all an employee of H.A.L. much less member of the above said Society.
The Society has already given up its rights therefore, the said Sri.
Thimmegowda cannot derive any right over the property.

But the said Thimmegowda in the second week of January- 2012 attempted to enter into the suit schedule property and on an enquiry, the plaintiff came to know that the said Thimmegowda on the basis of fraudulent and illegal allotment,
he started to claim right.
The plaintiff suspected the collusion between the Thimmegowda and Nalini Ashok thereby, approached the jurisdictional police, but he could not succeed in his attempt.

On the basis of the said illegal modified plan, Mr.
Thimmegowda and Society trying to put forth their false claim.

The B.D.A. issued Work Order on 17-03-2011 and stated in Clause No.16 that in case there is dispute regarding the title, B.D.A. has every right O S No.8246/2016 to cancel and modify the plan.

9. It is further alleged that the land measuring 4800 Sq.ft. in Sy.No.97/1-B also illegally grabbed by the Society.

In O.S.No.3902/2012 declaration for title about the suit schedule property has been sought and declaration also sought holding the modified plans of the B.D.A. in favour of Society as null and void and also sought for perpetual injunction.

However, the said site is said to be measuring East to West 46+92/2 feet and North to South 110 feet and totally measuring 7590 Sq.ft.
It is quite strange that how the site bearing No.2531 is said to be measuring only 6000 Sq.ft. and enlarged to 7590 Sq.ft.
Therefore, this itself indicates the false claim of the defendants.

10. It is further pleaded that the defendant No.6 claims to be an allottee directly from the Society in whose favour an absolute sale deed dated 29-08-2003 is executed by the Society in O S No.8246/2016 relation to site No.2532 measuring East to West 50 feet and North to South 100 feet.
The said defendant No.6 is trying to stake a claim to the said site as if it is carved out in a portion of schedule property.
The so called site No.2531 and 2532 are not at all in existence.
Thus, Sale Deeds are null and void, which do not affect the right of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property.
The plaintiff is in possession over the suit property.
But the defendants under the guise of said documents attempting to interfere to the plaintiff's possession.
The approach of the plaintiff to the jurisdictional police is went in vain.
Therefore, the plaintiff has left no option filed the present suit.
In view of the above said pleadings and allegations, the plaintiff sought for decretal of suit with cost.
The defendant No.6 placed ex-parte.
Whereas, defendants No.1 to 5 put in their appearance through their counsel and filed their written-statements.
The said defendants denied the plaint averments as false and contended that the suit is not maintainable either on law or on facts.

So, it deserves to be dismissed, since the plaintiff has M/S. Orange Tree vs K.V.Mathew on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20441790/
5 suppressed so many material facts.

It is specifically contended that the site bearing No.2531 'A'
Block of Singasandra Village, Begur Hobli formed by A.C.S. House Building Society as per the Bangalore Development Authority sanction plan and was allotted to its member Sri.
C.Chokkalingam.
The Society executed registered Sale Deed on 31-03-2004 in favour of Sri.
C.Chokkalingam and the said site is measuring East to West 60 feet and North to South 100 feet.
The said C.Chokkalingam was put in possession over the said property by means of Possession Certificate dated 10-04-2004.
Later, the society also issued No Objection Certificate.
The said C.Chokkalingam enjoyed the property and later by way of registered Sale Deed dated 17-05-2004.
The defendants obtained the khatha from the Bangalore Development Authority on 02-02-2010.
The khatha certificate are in their name and they are remitting the tax.
12. It is specifically contended that there was a marginal land, as such the Society executed Rectification Deed including the said marginal land by collecting the amount.
The BBMP after assessing the property given khatha No.1127/2531.

Therefore, the defendants are O S No.8246/2016 lawful owners and in possession of above said sites totally measuring 46+92/2x110 feet bounded by towards East-Site No.2532, towards West & North- Road and towards South-Private property,
which is said to be the property of the plaintiff.
The defendants are enjoying their property by exercising their rights as owners without any hindrance.
Further it is contended that in the year 2005 the plaintiff attempted to trespass in to the property therefore, the defendants filed O.S.No.8245/2005 against Smt. R.Nalini Ashok.
In the said suit, the present plaintiff attempted to implead as it is one of the party.
But the said application was not entertained.

The said suit decreed confirming the right, title and possession of the present defendants to the said property, which is O S No.8246/2016 hereinafter mentioned as written statement schedule property.
The said decree is enforceable against Smt. R.Nalini Ashok.

So, the plaintiff has no locus standi to file the present suit,
since it is hit by the provisions of Resjudicata.
The plaintiff is not in possession of the suit property so, suit for bare injunction is not maintainable.
The averments of plaint para No.3, 4 has been specifically denied.

It is contended that the khathas are all got up documents and created.
13.

It is contended that the land in Sy.No.97/1B was acquired by the Government.
The property of Yediyur Muniyamma was acquired by the government for and on behalf of Society and an award was passed.
Possession O S No.8246/2016
was taken and later delivered to the Society.
The Society by forming layout distributed sites to its members.
The Government acquired the land for the Society as per Notification dated 30-09-1989.
The averments of plaint para No.8 to 11 & 14 has been denied as false.
Further, it is contended that when Yediyur Muniyamma had no right or possession, the question of acquiring any rights by K.Damodar and putting Mohammed Jamil in possession does not arise.
14. It is also denied the averments of plaint para No.15 are as false.
It is contended that there is no relief sought against Mr. Thimmegowda and even the right, title and interest of the property of Thimmegowda has not been challenged in the present case.

The documents produced by the defendants O S No.8246/2016 demonstrates that the land in possession was included in the layout and hence, once the land is notified, the question of making any transaction without denotification has no sanctity in the eye of law.

17.

This defendant has paid an advance sale consideration amount of Rs.50,00,000/- to the defendants No.1 to 4 as per the Sale Agreement dated 10-08-2016 and the defendants No.1 to 4 agreed to construct the compound wall to the site at their own cost and also agreed to provide all the required documents O S No.8246/2016 agreed to receive the balance sale consideration during the time of registration of registered Sale Deed.

On the basis of pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor had framed the following ISSUES 1. Whether the plaintiff proves that he is in lawful possession of the schedule properties by virtue of the Sale Deed dated 28-02-2006 executed by Mrs. R.Nalini Ashok who was absolute owner as on the date of execution of the Sale Deed ?
O S No.8246/2016 2.

Whether the plaintiff proves the alleged interference by the defendants over the schedule property claiming to be the purchasers of the schedule property under one Chokkalingamma and defendant No.6 allottee of the site from the Society ?
3. What order or decree ?
19. The GPA holder of the plaintiff has been examined as PW-1 and relied upon 34 documents marked at Ex.P-1 to P-34 and closed the evidence.
20. On the other hand, the 4th defendant has deposed as DW-1 and he relied upon 41 documents marked at Ex.D-1 to D-41 and closed the evidence.
(During the cross-examination of PW-1, 08 documents have been marked by way of confronting the same).
The defendant No.5 has O S No.8246/2016 not deposed and even not produced any documents.
21. I have heard the arguments from the respective learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.

22. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
 ISSUE No.1 :: In the Negative  ISSUE No.2 :: In the Negative  ISSUE No.3 :: As per final order for the  following:-
 REASONS 23. ISSUE NO.1 :: It is the specific case of the plaintiff that the plaintiff-firm is in lawful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property since the plaintiff has been put in possession by virtue of registered Sale Deed O S No.8246/2016 dated 28-02-2006 executed by Smt. R. Nalini Ashok, who was the absolute owner of the schedule property on the date of execution of the said Sale Deed.
Accordingly, the General Power of Attorney holder of plaintiff-firm has deposed by reiterating the plaint averments.
In support of oral evidence, the said PW-1 has produced and relied upon 34 documents marked at Ex.P-1 to P-34.
So far as Ex.P-1 Special Power of Attorney is concerned, it has not been disputed by the defendants.

It is stated by the PW-1 that the suit property is carved out in Sy.No.97/1B of Singasandra Village, Begur Hobli, which has been converted as per order dated 21-09-1993 bearing No.
B-DIS.ALN.SR(S) 18/89-90 issued by the Special Deputy Commissioner, Bangalore O S No.8246/2016 District and its erstwhile khatha No.is 368, New Property No.308/97/1B measuring 17.5 guntas or 19,057.5 Square Feet.
As could be seen from the records, it is not in dispute that the land bearing Sy.No.97/1B was acquired by the Government.
On the contrary, the defendant No.4 deposed as DW-1 and denied that the plaintiff is the absolute owner and in possession of the suit schedule property.

25. It is stated by the PW-1 that the land Sy.No.97/1B totally measuring 0.22 guntas was basically belonging to one Mr. Naga Reddy, who is the father-in-law of Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma @
Ammayamma.
The said property was purchased by Mr. Naga Reddy through registered Sale Deed dated 17-04-1952.
After the death of Mr. Naga Reddy, his son Hanumappa Reddy succeeded the O S No.8246/2016 same and later, after his death, Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and her children succeeded the said property.
It is stated that the Government of Karnataka acquired the said land under an Acquisition Notification dated 30-09-1989 in favour of Aircraft Employees House Building Co- operative Society Ltd.,

26. It is also stated by the PW-1 that the Society was unable to take the possession of the property therefore, the said lands did not vest in favour of the said Society.

But, on the contrary, the said Smt.
Yediyur Muniyamma continued to remain in the possession.
In this connection, the said evidence has been specifically denied by the defendants.

To substantiate this particular evidence, there is no acceptable material O S No.8246/2016 evidence is placed by the plaintiff to hold that the said possession remained with the Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma, since the Society did not take possession.

Moreover, there is no evidence like order of denotification or any other order passed by the competent authority has been produced to believe that after having recalled the acquisition order,
the possession remained with Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma.
Therefore, this particular evidence of the plaintiff cannot be accepted to hold and believe that Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma retained the possession.
27. In this regard, the argument of the learned counsel for defendants that the said case of plaintiff is hit by Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 has to be accepted.

Because, the document at Ex.D-10 Land O S No.8246/2016 Acquisition Notification still remained intact and even Ex.D-12 clearly goes to show that consent award has been passed for having taken the possession by the said Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma.
These documents have not been rebutted by the plaintiff or Yediyur Muniyamma or any aggrieved person.
Hence, the case of the plaintiff that Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma retained the possession of the said property and she enjoyed the same holds no water at all.

28. The PW-1 states that the O.S.No.8577/1997, which was filed by Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and her children against the above said Society was ended in compromise and Society by way of Resolution dated 10-05-1999 abandoned and released its claim over 0.22 guntas in Sy.No.97/1B.

Further, the Society issued O S No.8246/2016 No Objection Certificate dated 05-06-1999 and also executed Deed of Settlement dated 23-05-1999 in favour of Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and others and even the same has been unanimously accepted by all member in its meeting by way of M/S. Orange Tree vs K.V.Mathew on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20441790/
9 Resolution dated 30-05-1999.
So, Smt.Yediyur Muniyamma became the absolute owner and in lawful possession of 0.22 guntas of converted lands.

In this regard, the plaintiff relied upon the Ex.P-10 the Proceedings of Society, Ex.P-11 certified copy of Deed of Settlement, Ex.P-12 the Proceedings of the said Society in the presence of its members.
The said documents no doubt clearly go to show that Society has released and abandoned its right over 0.22 guntas of land in Sy.No.97/1B in favour of Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and others.

But in my opinion, the said documents do not confer any right, title and interest over the suit property to Yediyur Muniyamma or in favour of anybody for the simple reason that the Yediyur Muniyamma and her children had already lost title over the said property by virtue of acquisition by the Government of Karnataka.
As I pointed out supra, the said notification has not been denotified and even it has not been reversed or cancelled or recalled by the competent authority.

It is evident that the said property was acquired for the purpose of Aircraft Society by the Government of Karnataka and the purpose of acquisition is to form a residential layout and not for any other purpose.
Under such circumstances, neither Society nor anybody can derive any right to deal with the same as per O S No.8246/2016 its whims and fancies.

Therefore, the case of the plaintiff that the Society abandoned its claim over 0.22 guntas of land in Sy.No.97/1B in favour of Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and others by way of Settlement Deed and Resolution does not remain for any consideration.

30. The PW-1 further states that Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and her children sold 17.5 guntas converted lands in Sy.No.97/1B, which is schedule property by way of registered Sale Deed dated 23-08-1999 in favour of Sri. K.Damodar for valuable consideration and put him in possession.
In this regard, the PW-1 relied upon Ex.P-13 certified copy of Sale Deed.

The said Sale Deed goes to show that Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma and her children sold the present suit property in favour of Sri.
K.Damodar.

It is evident from the O S No.8246/2016 records that when Smt.Yediyur Muniyamma and others had lost their right over the property of 0.22 guntas in Sy.No.97/1B, they cannot derive any title over the same by way of any document much less the document like Resolution and Settlement Deed to acquire the title again.

Hence, the question of transfer of title over the suit property by way of Sale Deed Ex.P-13 in favour of K.Damodar cannot be termed as valid transfer and cannot be accepted since the said document does not convey any kind of right in favour of Sri.
K.Damodar.
31.

It is also stated by the PW-1 that Sri. K.Damodar sold the suit schedule property in favour of Mr.
Sheik Mohammed Jamil and his wife Smt. Malika Mohammed Jamil through registered Sale Deed dated 20-11-2003 and put them in O S No.8246/2016 possession therefore, they enjoyed the property as absolute owners.
In this connection, PW-1 relied upon the Ex.P-19 certified copy of Sale Deed.
No doubt, the said document goes to show that for having sold the suit property by K.Damodar in favour of Sheik Mohammed Jamil.

But when Smt.Yediyur Muniyamma had no title she cannot transfer the same in favour of K.Damodar and even the said K. Damodar had no title to transfer the same in favour of Sheik Mohammed Jamil and Malika Mohammed Jamil.
Thus, the said sale deed does not confer any right, title or interest over the suit property.

It is also stated by the PW-1 that the said Mr. Sheik Mohammed Jamil and his wife Malika Mohammed Jamil sold the suit property in favour of Smt. R. Nalini Ashok by way of O S No.8246/2016 registered Sale Deed dated 10-09-2004 and she was put in possession.

The said Smt.
R.Nalini Ashok being absolute owner has sold the suit property in favour of plaintiff.
So, the plaintiff is in possession of the suit schedule property.
In support of the said oral evidence, the plaintiff relied upon the Sale Deed at Ex.P-23 dated 10-09-2004 and also relied upon Ex.P-3 Sale Deed dated 28-02-2006.

As I stated supra, Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma cannot get title over the suit property having been given the same to the Government under acquisition hence, the subsequent purchasers cannot transfer the right over the suit property much less to the plaintiff.

Hence, the whatever the oral and documentary evidence produced in this regard cannot be accepted to hold that the plaintiff has been in O S No.8246/2016 possession of the suit schedule property by virtue of Sale Deed at Ex.P-3.
33.

It is pertinent to note that, Ex.D-1 the plaint copy in O.S.No.3902/2012 goes to show that the present plaintiff had filed the said Original Suit against the Thimmegowda, agianst above said Society and against the Commissioner, B.D.A., Bangalore for seeking the relief of declaration and consequential relief of injunction in respect of the present suit schedule property including the another property bearing Sy.No.97/1B measuring 4800 Sq.ft.
No doubt, the said fact has been narrated by the plaintiff in the present plaint.
In the said suit, one Mr. Thimmegowda, who is the allottee of site from the Society contested the suit, which can be seen at Ex.D-2.

Ex .D-3 Judgment in O.S.No.3902/2012 O S No.8246/2016 goes to show that the XLI Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge,
Bangalore (CCH-42) dismissed the suit by rejecting the plaint holding that the court does not have any jurisdiction to entertain the suit, since the said court has no jurisdiction to question the acquisition made by the Government.

R.Nalini Ashok for the relief of perpetual injunction for the property site No.2531 carved out of Sy.No.97/1B of Singasandra Village, which can be seen at Ex.D-7.

sentences.text: held that the plaintiffs have established their possession over the site No.2531 and it is evident that the said property is written statement schedule property in the present case.

It is seen from the said document that in the said case, Smt.
R. Nalini Ashok claimed right over the present suit property and even contended that the site No.2531 is part of the present suit property.
It is necessary to state that there is no records to believe that the said judgment has been reversed.

Therefore, it appears from the above said documents at Ex.D-1 to 3 that present plaintiff had also claimed right over the site, which was allotted to Mr.
Thimmegowda by the Society claiming that the said site area is part of the present suit property and even as I said O S No.8246/2016 supra, Smt. R.Nalini Ashok also claimed the site of the present defendants and they have not succeeded.

Therefore, from these documents, it can be safely held that the plaintiff is still attempting to get create right over the suit schedule property on the basis of right,
which is said to have been accrued in favour of Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma through the Society under different documents in the absence of any denotification.

11 35.
No doubt, there is a Rectification Deed between the Society and the defendants in respect of acquisition of property by the defendants to the additional measurement of 1590 Sq.ft.
But the said weakness cannot be made use as a trump card by the plaintiff to seek the relief of permanent injunction.
Moreover, O S No.8246/2016 the PW-1 during his cross-examination pleaded ignorance about the existence of site No.2531, which falls within the boundaries of Sy.No.97/1B.
There are no documents to believe that the property of the defendants falls within the present suit property.
No doubt, no worthwhile has been extracted from the mouth of PW-1.

But the oral and documentary evidence placed by the plaintiff cannot be accepted to hold that the plaintiff has acquired the suit property and in possession from its previous vendor Smt. R.Nalini Ashok.
36. It is evident that the number of sale deeds right from Smt. Yediyur Muniyamma till the sale deed at Ex.P-3 have been executed in respect of suit property without there being any right.
Under such circumstances, from the above O S No.8246/2016 said reasons, it is held that the plaintiff utterly failed to prove the Issue No.1 and accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the negative.
37. ISSUE NO.2 :: It is held above that the plaintiff failed to establish the possession over the suit schedule property.
Under such circumstances, the question of alleged interference by the defendants does not arise.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 in the negative.

38. ISSUE NO.3 :: In view of my findings on Issue No.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The suit filed by the plaintiff is dismissed.
Parties are directed to bear their own cost.
O S No.8246/2016 Draw decree accordingly.
